group: q|what is a top 1% ironman finish time

result.why: No credible source publishes a 99th-percentile (top 1%) finish time for full-distance IRONMAN finishers, either for the whole field or by sex. The best peer-reviewed source is Knechtle et al. 2025 in Sports Medicine - Open (PMC11953511). It covers 687,696 IRONMAN age-group finishes from 2002 to 2022 (553,608 men, 134,088 women), downloaded from ironman.com. Its Table 1 gives only a mean, SD, minimum and maximum for each sex and 5-year age group (for example, men 30-34: n 78,919, mean 12:15:21, SD 1:46:16, min 8:07:22). It reports no whole-field or per-sex mean or SD and no medians or percentiles. That leaves 24 age-by-sex cells and no single distribution that matches the question. The only source with whole-field percentiles is tritimes.org/stats/average-ironman-time. It reports 799,233 finisher results from 501 races, 2002-2026: top 10% under 10:07:36, top 25% under 11:05:44, median 12:23:21; men's median 12:12:49, women's median 13:07:37. It gives no top-1% figure, though, and the site names no operator and does not say where its data comes from, so it fails the source standard. The other pages found (Marathon Handbook, Triathlon Loop, Tri247, trinewbies) are blogs that quote averages without raw data. A credible top-1% value would have to be computed from the official IRONMAN results archive, which is outside this task.
result.caveat: Reference points for a follow-up. Knechtle et al. 2025 has mean and SD by sex and age group only, from IRONMAN age-group finishers 2002-2022; it excludes professionals, and the times are right-skewed with a hard 17-hour cutoff, so percentiles should not be derived from mean and SD. Tritimes (operator and data provenance not stated) gives p50 12:23:21 and top 10% under 10:07:36 for all finishers 2002-2026. Professional winning times are about 7:20 to 8:30, and those would sit far above the 99th percentile of the full field. If this metric is added later, it would be new (not in the catalogue): id ironman_time, unit seconds, direction low, format time_hm, population IRONMAN full-distance finishers.
